PITTSBURGH


, Oct. 16, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / --[Viatris Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4800024-1&h=4098608231&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.viatris.com%2Fen&a=Viatris+Inc.) (Nasdaq: VTRS), a global healthcare company, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75%) for the treatment of presbyopia in adults. RYZUMVI is currently approved in the United States for the treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis and is the only commercially available FDA-approved product for that use. This approval expands the product's indications to include presbyopia.


Viatris is exploring the potential for a partner in the United States to commercialize RYZUMVI for the treatment of presbyopia.


**About Opus Genetics and Viatris Collaboration** Opus Genetics and Viatris Inc. (through an affiliated entity) are parties to a global licensing agreement which provides for the development of phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% and grants exclusive rights to Viatris to commercialize the product in the United States.


**About Presbyopia** Presbyopia is the gradual loss of near focusing ability due to aging, that typically becomes noticeable in the early to mid-40s. It is a nearly universal condition that, when uncorrected, contributes significantly to vision-related disability. Presbyopia leads to symptoms like eye strain and blurred near vision, impacting daily tasks and productivity.


**INDICATIONS AND USAGE** RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution) 0.75% is indicated for:


- Treatment of presbyopia in adults
- Treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis produced by adrenergic agonists (e.g., phenylephrine) or parasympatholytic agents (e.g., tropicamide) in adults and pediatric patients 3 years of age and older


**IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION**


**Warnings and Precautions** **Uveitis:** RYZUMVI is not recommended to be used in patients with active ocular inflammation (e.g., iritis).
**Potential for Eye Injury or Contamination:** To avoid the potential for eye injury or contamination, care should be taken to avoid touching the vial tip to the eye or to any other surface.
**Use with Contact Lenses:** Contact lens wearers should be advised to remove their lenses prior to the instillation of RYZUMVI and wait 10 minutes after dosing before reinserting their contact lenses.


**Adverse Reactions** **Presbyopia** The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were conjunctival hyperemia (21%) and instillation site irritation (16%).
**Pharmacologically-induced Mydriasis** The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were instillation site discomfort including pain, stinging, and burning (16%) and conjunctival hyperemia (12%). The only non-ocular adverse reaction reported in > 5% of subjects was dysgeusia (6%). The majority of the adverse reactions were mild, transient and self-resolving.
